sections.section: About the Data — validation and purpose
sections.text: AirNow observations receive preliminary checks but do not undergo the complete validation and certification process associated with regulatory AQS submissions. AirNow communicates AQI to the public; it does not establish regulatory compliance. This methodological distinction cannot certify any individual historical observation.

AirNow reporting includes acquisition and processing delays. A displayed observation time can describe an earlier sampling interval rather than the moment a user reads the page. Use supplied interval boundaries and acquisition timestamps; do not infer present conditions from an old reading.

sections.text: An AQS monitor identity combines the geographic site, pollutant parameter and Parameter Occurrence Code (POC). Different instruments measuring the same pollutant at one site can have different POCs. A site alone is therefore not a complete monitor identity.

A pollutant standard specifies an averaging duration and statistical form. EPA summary calculations depend on the applicable standard, and the same underlying measurements can produce several different summaries. A simple selected-station range or arithmetic mean does not establish attainment of a standard.

sections.section: What is the U.S. Air Quality Index / How does the AQI work?
sections.text: The AQI is an index for communicating outdoor air quality and associated health concern. Its categories convey increasing concern as the index rises. An AQI index value is not a pollutant concentration with physical units; preserve the supplied measurement type rather than treating them interchangeably.
